claim_one_line: 2T CANNOT HOLD THE BIT -- and the 'door' attribution this arc was written to make was REFUTED BY ITS OWN CONTROL, which is recorded rather than dropped. (1) THE REAL CONTENT: 2T built by closure from (i,j,omega), order 24; over ALL 576 pairs kappa takes EXACTLY three values {-2, 0, 2} (24/384/168), so 2-kappa in {4,2,0}, class D in {+1,2,0}, and THE CLASS -1 -- THE BIT -- NEVER OCCURS ANYWHERE IN 2T (eps = -1 needs kappa-2 a positive perfect square; 2T's kappa-2 in {-4,-2,0} never is). This is a property of the GROUP, not of any map into it. (2) The fig-8 relator w x w^-1 = y, w = x^-1 y x y^-1, has 72 solutions in 2T of which 48 GENERATE -- reproducing the banked surjection count (B237/B1019/B997) from the relator alone, the arc's control that group and relator are right. (3) THE FAILED ATTRIBUTION: a draft headlined 'all 48 surjections give kappa = 0, so THE DOOR is not class-preserving'. The discriminating control refutes it -- ALL 384 GENERATING PAIRS of 2T already have kappa = 0, so the relator cuts NOTHING and kappa = 0 on the surjections is a fact about GENERATION IN 2T, not about the figure-eight relator or the door. Correct statement, weaker and more general: any surjection from any group onto 2T sends a generating pair to class D = 2, and with (1), 2T cannot carry the bit HOWEVER one maps into it. The conclusion survives; the door-specific framing does not. (4) RAMIFICATION, two facts with NO map between them: the object's algebra (5,-5) is split everywhere; 2T's is (-1,-1), the HURWITZ quaternions, ramified at exactly {2, oo} (Hilbert symbols; controls matching known answers both ways). A draft said 'the door ADDS ramification' -- REMOVED: no map between the two algebras is exhibited, so a causal reading is exactly the T-IDENTIFICATION-IS-AN-INPUT error. The facts are recorded side by side with nothing claimed to flow between them. FENCED: SU(2) is NOT derived -- 2T sits inside SU(2) by construction. kappa is not a homomorphism invariant. No measured value. Gate 5 clean.
